title: backpressure-sandbox-weekly-diary-2026-08-23
content:
Weekly diary — Backpressure Sandbox (notes + action items)

Date: 2026-08-23 standup / sandbox sync (followups 8/25)
Owner: Aisha Raman
Context: mini-experiment series in the sandbox cluster (sbox-03) to validate a conservative backpressure gate and a coalesce-window reduction on microkernel handshake. Goal: reduce queue tail amplification during brief spikes without hurting steady-state throughput.

Summary (TL;DR)
- Ran three chained experiments this week. Early wins on p99 smoothing but saw p95 regression on mixed short/long workloads after patch X.
- KV soft-eviction heuristics interact badly with small coalesce windows under heavy interleaving — causing unexpected re-reads and stall cycles.
- Action items assigned: repro script (Benji), kernel revert candidate + small fixes (Claire), longer bake + telemetry adjustments (Mateo).

What we ran (sandbox details)
- Baseline: microkernel-v2.3 (current prod-closest), coalesce-window=8ms, slot-allocator=default, kv-evict-threshold=0.65. 12 runs, 10m each. Traffic mix: 70% short-chat (<64 tokens), 30% long-completion (>512).
- Exp A (backpressure-gate-01): introduce conservative gate that starts rejecting coalescing if inflight queue > 1200 requests. coalesce-window kept at 8ms. 8 runs.
- Exp B (coalesce-4ms + backpressure-gate-01): coalesce-window=4ms with same gate. 10 runs.
- Exp C (coalesce-4ms + gate + kv-soft-evict-tweak): reduce kv eviction aggressiveness (0.8 -> 0.92 factor). 6 runs.

High level observations
- Exp A: p95 improved ~10% on short-only synthetic traffic; steady-state throughput unchanged. p99 slightly better for brief spikes.
- Exp B: steady throughput dropped ~14% for mixed workload; observed frequent KV cache thrash where threads re-requested large KV slices several times. p95 increased from 68ms -> 120ms on mixed runs (notable).
- Exp C: bumping the kv-soft-evict threshold reduced re-reads but did not fully restore throughput; p95 back to ~82ms, p99 remains improved vs baseline.

Root-cause hypothesis (working)
- Small coalesce windows reduce opportunities to form larger batches which increases per-request overheads; combined with backpressure gate this increases churn in the KV cache: more partial KV hits, more KV prefill wakeups, which can queue up work for the microkernel handshake.
- The eviction heuristics are tuned for longer coalesce windows; with 4ms window the heuristic evicts slightly earlier than optimal causing re-population costs.
- There is also evidence of a scheduling hotspot: when gate trips, a bunch of requests are rerouted into the short-path reorderer and cause lock contention on the prefill coordinator (see logs).

Interesting traces / artifacts to inspect
- trace-id sbox-20260823-17-9a3: p95 spike aligned with KV re-read sequence. (see linked PR and trace in dashboards)
- flamegraph sbox-20260823-expb.svg (attached in sandbox artifacts) — shows increased wall time in handshake->kv_fill.
- telemetry: slot allocator queue depth correlates with p95 slope (weight ~0.6)

Repro steps (quick) — Benji to own and expand
1) start sandbox with microkernel-v2.3 + experiment flags (--coalesce-ms=4 --backpressure-gate=1200 --kv-evict=0.65)
2) replay mixed trace (mixed-70-30-aug-trace.json) at 1.2x arrival rate for 10 minutes
3) collect traces, prometheus (req_latency_p95/p99), and kv_hit_ratio by slice
4) reproduce exp C by adjusting kv-evict to 0.92 and compare
Notes: local repro uses sbox-image:sha-202608-3, follow the reproduce.sh in /sandbox/backpressure/

Decisions made in sync
- Do not roll out coalesce-window=4ms to any dedicated cluster yet. Needs further instrumented runs.
- Prioritize two fixes: (1) tighten prefill coordinator locks to avoid thundering herd; (2) add a conservative backpressure metric that considers KV hit-rate before gating (Claire will prototype).
- Add an experiment to test adaptive coalesce window that grows when KV hit-rate dips below threshold; low-risk A/B in sandbox only.

Action items
- Benji: author repro script and run expanded mixed-run matrix (done by 2026-08-26). Deliverable: reproducible runs + raw traces pushed under sbox-03/artifacts/backpressure-20260823.tar.gz.
- Claire: prepare kernel-branch with two small changes: prefill-lock-slim and gated-kv-metric hook. Put draft PR by 2026-08-25. Link PR -> RDW-2750.
- Mateo: update telemetry dashboards to show per-slice kv-populate count and a coalesce-success metric. ETA 2026-08-28.
- Renee: run a low-volume dry-run on dedicated-dev-1 next week to sanity-check behavior (ETA 2026-08-30).
- Aisha: consolidate notes and schedule deeper post-mortem if Exp C still shows >10% regression after Claire's PR.

Open questions / to validate
- Is the microkernel handshake spend amplified by specific model families (decoder-only vs encoder-decoder)? Early signs: decoder-only workloads (gpt-like) show more sensitivity. Need two model families tested.
- Could slot-allocator policy be adapted to prioritize small-wait requests during gate conditions? Tradeoff unknown.
- Are there net cost implications of leaving coalesce-window higher to preserve KV locality? Need a quick unit cost calc (tokens/sec vs GPU seconds) — product asked for a rough number.

Notes to self (informal)
- Quick thought: if we can detect KV coldness early (a rapid drop in hit-rate for a cohort) we can bump coalesce window up temporarily to rebuild locality. Might interact badly with latency SLO for short requests though.
- Keep an eye on the reorderer when gate trips — I think the gate currently redirects to path B which has a sleep(1ms) backoff that compounds under load.
- Slack thread for the day had some good ideas from SRE about sampling prefill requests instead of full re-population. Worth a spike.

Meeting notes (8/23 sync)
- Attendees: Aisha, Benji, Claire, Mateo, Renee, Tom (SRE attending briefly)
- Tom recommended adding a sampled prefill trace to reduce telemetry overhead — we agreed.
- Claire proposed a small refactor to allow kv-evict-policy to be pluggable at runtime — appetite: high.
- Quick consensus: experiments continue in sandbox, no dedicated rollouts.

Appendix — quick metrics snapshot (representative run numbers)
- Baseline mixed-run (avg over 12 runs): throughput 11.9k tokens/s, p95 68ms, p99 195ms, kv_hit_ratio 0.87
- Exp A: throughput 11.8k tokens/s, p95 61ms, p99 170ms, kv_hit_ratio 0.86
- Exp B: throughput 10.2k tokens/s, p95 120ms, p99 240ms, kv_hit_ratio 0.71
- Exp C: throughput 11.0k tokens/s, p95 82ms, p99 182ms, kv_hit_ratio 0.83

Files referenced/where to find artifacts
- sbox-03:/artifacts/backpressure/2026-08-23/ (traces, flamegraphs, raw-prometheus)
- PR draft: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1849
- Jira: RDW-2718 (backpressure sandbox orchestration), RDW-2750 (kernel prefill fixes)
- Confluence sketch: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SRV/Backpressure+Sandbox

Final thought: small coalesce windows + naive gating is a neat idea but the cache dynamics are the dominant factor. Need to instrument the KV layer aggressively and run controlled experiments that isolate coalesce-window from eviction policy.

-- end diary entry --

(Will update after Benji's reproducer runs on 8/26 and Claire's PR lands.)
